name: Temporary Stay for Self-Employment / Business Ownership

requirements.blocker_text: Requires registering a Croatian business (typically a d.o.o./j.d.o.o. limited-liability company or an obrt sole proprietorship) and demonstrating financial viability through a business plan and proof of initial capital.
requirements.fix_path: Register a qualifying Croatian business entity and prepare a business plan.

evidence_required.document: Proof of ongoing financial viability at renewal

sources.title: Croatian Parliament -- Aliens Act (Official Gazette No. 133/2020, as amended 114/22, 151/22), general work/self-employment provisions

notes: NEW ROUTE, part of Croatia's initial build. STATUS SET TO DRAFT, deliberately, because this pass could not confirm current, euro-denominated figures at tier-1: no specific minimum investment amount, no minimum number of Croatian employees to hire, and no minimum owner-salary threshold were found in the Aliens Act excerpt retrieved, nor in mup.gov.hr's work-of-third-country-nationals page (which addresses self-employed individuals only as one of several labour-market-test exemption categories, without figures). Several tier-3/4 sources (law-firm and expat blogs) cite older, pre-euro figures denominated in Croatian kuna (e.g. 200,000-300,000 kn investment, hiring 3 Croatian nationals) dating to before Croatia's January 2023 euro adoption -- these are NOT used here since they are both outdated and not tier-1; they are noted only as context that a real, more demanding version of this route likely exists and should be revisited if a current tier-1 or tier-3 source with euro figures surfaces. Only the confirmed, non-quantified requirement (registration + business plan + capital) is encoded as hard, consistent with validate.py's rule that draft-status routes get a warning rather than a failure for weaker sourcing. work_rights set to 'restricted' (schema enum: self-employment in the registered business only, not open local employment); study_rights 'none' (no study entitlement described); family_can_join set true on the general basis that hr_residence_permit_family_reunification confirms temporary-stay holders (a category this route falls under) can sponsor family members, not from a business-route-specific source; duration_length left as an explicit 'not specified' string rather than a guessed figure.
